erdStudio.projectPath.markdownDescription: Folder that holds your ERD Studio data (`erdStudio.semanticDir` is created inside it). Usually a dbt project root, and auto-detected from the workspace when empty — but any folder works, with or without `dbt_project.yml`; without one there is no dbt manifest to compare against. Absolute, or relative to a workspace folder. Changing this requires a window reload.

erdStudio.semanticDir.description: Folder, relative to the project, that holds ERD Studio's tables and diagrams. Changing this requires a window reload.

erdStudio.claudeSync.skipPermissions.markdownDescription: When **Execute with Claude** launches Claude Code to apply a sync plan, pass `--dangerously-skip-permissions` so it edits files without asking. Off by default: Claude Code prompts before each file change. The launch command is always shown for confirmation first. Read from your user settings only: a workspace's `.vscode/settings.json` cannot turn it on.

erdStudio.feedback.aiAssist.markdownDescription: Let the Feedback dialog make **one** request to a language model to draft a title, pick bug vs feature, and check for duplicate issues. Only what you typed is sent — diagnostics, file paths and model names never are. Your own model is used where VS Code has one (VS Code asks for access itself, once); otherwise `#erdStudio.feedback.endpoint#`, or — if `#erdStudio.feedback.hostedFallback#` is on — a relay run by the extension author that forwards your description to a named third-party AI provider under the author's account. That last one always asks first and names both. Turn this off to make no request at all.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Your editor's language model first, then `#erdStudio.feedback.endpoint#`, then the ERD Studio service. The old default; still honoured, no longer offered in the dialog.
Only your editor's own language model. Nothing is sent anywhere else; if this editor has none, the Feedback dialog simply shows no analysis.
Only `#erdStudio.feedback.endpoint#`, with the key you stored via **ERD Studio: Set Feedback API Key**. Not offered in the dialog unless you have already picked it here.

Only the small relay run by the extension author, which forwards your description to a third-party AI provider under the author's account. Pick this if you have Copilot but would rather not spend it on triaging feedback. Requires `#erdStudio.feedback.hostedFallback#` to be on, and asks before the first request.
erdStudio.feedback.provider.markdownDescription: Which model triages your feedback. The Feedback dialog offers two: your editor’s own model, or the ERD Studio service. Each pins one destination and does **not** fall through — if the one you pick is unavailable here, the dialog says so and offers the other rather than quietly sending your text somewhere you did not choose. `auto` (the old default, your own model first) and `endpoint` still work if you set them here, but the dialog no longer offers them.

erdStudio.feedback.hostedFallback.markdownDescription: As a last resort — when VS Code offers no language model and `#erdStudio.feedback.endpoint#` is empty — allow the Feedback dialog to send your description to a small relay run by the extension author, which forwards it to a third-party AI provider under the author's account and that provider's terms. You are always asked first — the prompt names the relay and the provider — and the request carries only what you typed. Turn this off to keep feedback analysis on your own model or endpoint only.

erdStudio.feedback.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API for feedback analysis (e.g. `https://api.openai.com/v1`). Leave empty to use VS Code's built-in language model when one is available. The API key is stored in secret storage via **ERD Studio: Set Feedback API Key**, never in settings.

erdStudio.feedback.trackReports.markdownDescription: Show a **My Reports** view listing issues you filed from ERD Studio, refreshed from GitHub every few hours. Requires you to be signed in to GitHub in VS Code; the view is hidden otherwise and you are never prompted to sign in.

erdStudio.telemetry.enabled.markdownDescription: Send one anonymous usage heartbeat a day, plus at most three same-day interim copies in an install's first week, the week after a major update or on a day with an error: which ERD Studio features were used and how often, bucketed project sizes and error counts — never names, paths, file contents or error messages. This setting can only turn telemetry **off**: VS Code's `#telemetry.telemetryLevel#` must also allow it, and nothing is sent when that is `off`. See [Telemetry](https://github.com/liam-machine/erd-studio/blob/main/telemetry/README.md) for every field sent and how long it is kept.

erdStudio.checkKnownFixes.markdownDescription: When ERD Studio hits an error that a newer release already fixes, say so and offer **Update**. The first error in a session downloads the list of known fixes (once a day at most) from ERD Studio's server; the request carries nothing about you, your project or the error — the list is matched on your machine. Works whether or not `#erdStudio.telemetry.enabled#` is on.

erdStudio.startSuggestions.markdownDescription: When a folder with no diagram opens and ERD Studio finds an obvious start in it (CREATE TABLE scripts, a Power BI or Fabric semantic model, a DBML file), offer once to create the diagram from it; when you open the Diagrams view of a folder with nothing to start from, say so and show how to bring in a data model from Databricks, Snowflake, Power BI or Fabric. Closing either asks again in a later window, at most three times per folder. Set this to `false` in a repository's `.vscode/settings.json` to turn it off for everyone who opens it, or in your user settings to turn it off everywhere. **ERD Studio: Turn Off Start Suggestions for This Folder** turns it off for one folder on this machine only.

erdStudio.dbml.offerConvert.markdownDescription: When you open a diagram in a YAML/JSON project, offer once a session to convert it to DBML. Your project keeps working as it is either way; turn this off to stop the offer in every workspace. **ERD Studio: Convert Project to DBML** still works from the Command Palette.

enumDescriptions: Ask each time, with Update, Always and Never.
Update the files that point at it without asking.
Leave every file as it is, and ask nothing. A file moved where ERD Studio does not read it is still pointed out.
erdStudio.dbml.updateReferencesOnMove.markdownDescription: When you move or rename a `.dbml` file (or a folder of them) in the Explorer in a DBML project, update the diagrams and relationships files that point at it: their `use` lines, and the table's schema (`Table crm.fct_order`) when it lands in another schema folder. Renaming a table file renames the table everywhere, since its file name is its name. Each update is one step for **Edit > Undo**. **Move Table…** and **Move Diagram to Layer…** always update them, whatever this says.

erdStudio.import.timeLimitSeconds.markdownDescription: How long **Import SQL DDL…** may spend reading your scripts, in seconds. Reading runs in the background with a progress notification you can cancel. When the time is up (or you press **Cancel**), the tables read so far are imported and the draft's **Not imported** list says where reading stopped in each file. `0` means no limit.

enumDescriptions: Quiet rows: beside each name, only what is unusual or tells it apart (a warehouse name that differs, a table on no diagram, tables from other layers, a problem). Counts, owners and which diagrams show a table are in each row's hover.
Every detail beside every name: how many diagrams, tables, schemas and relationships each row holds, each table's owner and how many diagrams show it.
erdStudio.sidebar.rowDetails.markdownDescription: How much the rows of the **Diagrams**, **Table Library** and **Relationships** views say beside their names. **Show Row Details** and **Hide Row Details**, in each view's **…** menu, switch it.

enumDescriptions: Curved lines: soft curves that go around tables. Where two lines cross, the one underneath is cut; where a line has to pass under a table, a faint dashed line shows its way.
Square lines that go around tables, with a small hop where two lines cross.
erdStudio.canvas.lineStyle.markdownDescription: How diagrams draw their relationship lines. **Curved** and **Hops**, in the diagram's toolbar, switch it for every diagram.
